questions.stem: A flask contains hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio of $2: 1$ by mass at temperature $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The ratio of average kinetic energy per molecule of hydrogen and oxygen respectively is :
questions.solution: The mean translational kinetic energy per molecule of an ideal gas is $3k_BT/2$. Both gases have the same temperature, so their mean energies are equal and the ratio is $1:1$.

questions.stem: A monoatomic gas of molar mass $m$ is kept in a insulated container. Container is moving with velocity $v$. If the container is suddenly stopped, then the change in the temperature of the gas is
questions.solution: For one mole, the lost bulk kinetic energy is $\tfrac12mv^2$. In the idealized insulated rigid container it becomes internal energy, so $\tfrac32R\Delta T=\tfrac12mv^2$. Hence $\Delta T=mv^2/(3R)$.
